Round 2, Jan Beṯ-Şawoce. English quotations below reproduce the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation. Analyses and sense distinctions rest on the Turoyo. Round-one proposals are retained as the comparison baseline and are not republished in this JSON.

Jan 3.27/695 explicitly quotes liturgical speech: Yoldaṯ Aloho bṯəlto and the address to Mary supply the context for feminine ṭrudi. The source has d rather than glossary ḏ; no normalisation or native Turoyo base form is reconstructed.

The phrase w ayna d bi šəršo ḥəqle ṭrudi mene concerns removing the evil one from an afflicted person. m- source marking matches the semantic frame of expulsion, but the mixed/liturgical register limits what can be inferred about Turoyo valency.

No example is added to a new Imperativ box. The quoted form is retained in this research note and the occurrence decision as evidence of register contact, with no change to round-one intransitive motion sense 2.
Is rapidity a lexical component of intransitive ṭrḏ, or contextual to the mount journey in 29/78? One attestation establishes motion and valency more securely than speed.

Confirm that ṭrudi and its surrounding prayer are quoted Syriac rather than an adapted native Turoyo Imperativ. If native Turoyo has a corresponding feminine form, establish it independently before creating an Imperativ box.

The quoted Syriac prayer applies expulsion to the evil one with mene marking the afflicted person from whom he is driven. This is a spiritual participant extension of expulsion for comparison, not a new Turoyo sense or an attestation of native Turoyo Imperativ morphology.
